findings.text: the resolution is triggered by the leaf's own is_symlink() only, so a protected path whose ancestor is a symlink still emits an unlaunchable destination: probed on this host with the fence's own binary, "bwrap --dev-bind / / --ro-bind <home>/.config/reckon <home>/.config/reckon" exits 1 ("bwrap: Can't mkdir <home>/.config/reckon: No such file or directory") while the identical bind with a real parent exits 0, and binding the resolved target instead seals a write through the symlinked-parent path with EROFS — so the repair is complete for the shape this node was dispatched against, but a home with ~/.config symlinked (a shape this workstation already has for ~/.gitconfig) would still abort every fenced launch.

the "emits no bind when the target already lies inside another protected path" clause is asserted only as the absence of the link's path from argv, so deleting the _within_any skip at reckon/_backends.py:1959 — which would emit a redundant --ro-bind of a target inside an already-sealed directory — leaves the suite green; the effect is benign (bubblewrap accepts the duplicate bind) but the clause the done_when names has no observable of its own.

the recorded lint figure does not reconstruct under the instrument it names: ruff (root venv, repo config) over the two touched paths on the complete reviewed worktree reports 6 findings at head, none of them inside the ranges the commit added, so the delta claim (no findings added) holds by measurement while the absolute "8" names no runnable instrument and no lint log is carried beside the gate logs; the same figure appears at :241 from the earlier run, so the absolute number is best read as copied forward and the delta as the claim that was actually established.

item_verdicts.done_when: every clause of the SPEC is present and proven by a test that executes the composed argv rather than inspecting its shape — the resolution, the refusal when the resolution is removed, and the "emits no bind when the target already lies inside another protected path" clause — and I re-derived each rather than reading it (tests/test_launch_plan_fences_the_home.py:387 launches the symlinked home, :416-419 shows the write through each link refused by the read-only overlay, and the file's own declared-mutation hook (_RED_LOGS["symlink-resolution"], :450-466) re-run from the reviewed tree exits 1 with the stub never running).
item_verdicts.goal: the goal — a fenced launch composes a runnable argv when a protected path is a symlink — is delivered and executed: reckon/_backends.py:1930 protected_read_only_binds resolves a symlinked protected entry to its resolved target and fence_argv at :2012 emits that destination, I re-ran the reviewed gate file at head (4 passed, 0 skipped, bwrap present), and the real-home composition log carries this host's own ~/.gitconfig — a symlink into ~/Code/dotfiles/git/gitconfig — as its resolved target with the stub exiting 0, so the defect the node reports reproduces here and is gone at the head.

item_verdicts.write_paths: the nine files changed across dc52fa08 and 72e0ff48 all lie inside the five declared write paths (reckon/_backends.py, tests/test_launch_plan_fences_the_home.py, docs/figures/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home/*, docs/plans/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home.html, docs/evidence/archive/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home-landed.html), nothing outside them is touched, and the reviewed worktree is clean at head 72e0ff48.

justifications.durability: the fences are asserted: tests/test_launch_plan_fences_the_home.py:404 asserts no --ro-bind destination is a symlink, :410-419 executes the fence and shows the write refused through both links, and :441-447 makes the failure mode reachable by asserting the mutation applied before requiring the refusal; the deduction is the clause at :407, where a regression that skipped the inside-protected-path check and bound the target redundantly would still pass (measured: an extra bind of an already-sealed file is accepted by bubblewrap), so that clause's guard is nominal.
justifications.evidence: the gate measures the done_when by launching the fenced argv and asserting the refusal, and its result is recorded beside its base arm with a corrected revision header; one clause of the done_when, "emits no bind when the target already lies inside another protected path", is asserted only as the link's absence from argv (:407) rather than by any observable of the duplicate bind it forbids, so the gate does not fully measure what the done_when names.
justifications.fit: protected_read_only_binds sits beside protected_paths and reuses the module's own idiom (_within_any, the (source, destination) bind pair, the exists() filter), ruff reports the same findings at head as at base with none inside the added ranges, the two new tests follow the file's existing negative-control shape instead of inventing a second one, and the naming checks find no plan label or ticket reference in the changed files or symbols.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the named defect is fixed and executed (tests/test_*_home.py:387, and the real-home composition exits 0), but the resolution trigger at reckon/_backends.py:1954 tests the leaf's own is_symlink() only, so the adjacent shape — a protected path whose *ancestor* is the symlink, e.g. a symlinked ~/.config — still composes an argv bubblewrap refuses, which my probe measured (see the finding at that line).
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff is exactly the five declared paths' subject matter — one production function plus its call wiring, the test file that exercises it, the figure logs, the plan comment block and the archive record — nothing outside them is touched, no unrelated file is reformatted, and the worktree is clean at head 72e0ff48.
